title: C310B — Restraints control module connector reference
introduction:
The restraints control module (RCM) uses sensor and occupant information to decide which deployable restraints are needed. This connector reference maps its recorded connections to pretensioners, inflatable curtains and sensors. I read the function labels carefully: driver and passenger, input and deployment circuit, and positive and negative are meaningful distinctions, not spare words in a wiring alphabet soup.

Start with the connector identity and harness heading, locate a printed cavity label in the drawing, then read the matching table row across. Numbering runs downward within vertical columns, with wider gaps between some columns. Gray-filled positions match blank circuit entries where those rows are supplied. The surrounding outline shows housing features; it does not identify a release movement.

This page supports identification, not hands-on restraint testing. Physical viewing direction, access, depowering, test setup and restoration are outside this reference. Size and gauge conventions are not defined here, and repeated terminal entries do not establish which version applies. The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions in the drawing. That discrepancy remains unresolved and does not establish extra physical cavities.

items.name: Qualified service and prescribed methods
items.detail: Pyrotechnic-component service is restricted to qualified personnel. Any hands-on airbag or pretensioner work requires the applicable restraint-specific depowering, handling, test-equipment and restoration procedures. This connector map supplies none of those sequences; do not substitute a generic jumper or resistance test.

edits.why: The harness identifier ties the face drawing to its accompanying identification table. Use the printed cavity labels to navigate; gaps between columns are not positions to count, and the connector's gender does not establish the physical viewing direction.

Keep each circuit number, color and function together when reading a row. Driver/passenger and positive/negative labels distinguish connections that must not be interchanged. Repeated cavity rows preserve different recorded gauge or terminal entries without identifying their applicability. Blank circuit rows are unassigned entries in this reference, not evidence that the restraint system has passed a check.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata gives Pin Count as 66, while the attached face drawing shows numbered positions through 60. Confirm the intended count and drawing association; the supplied evidence does not explain the difference.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 87 primary units, four complete pages/one figure and two edits. Original first CLI author covered 57 units/two headings. Complete draft explicitly discloses the count discrepancy and covers all table rows and raw text. Original partial author retained separately; physical count and unqualified gauge/terminal alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
